beef242ca8.why: The three-operand VEX comparison can read xmm6 directly, eliminating the copy into xmm7 while preserving the full YMM results.

356ee63d33.why: All seven instructions produce a required vector result or store, and AVX2 cannot merge these independent operations.

17ca74b518.why: Each instruction writes a distinct required vector result, with no redundant copy or operation to remove.

59a6de4675.why: AVX2 needs both operations for (ymm1 & ymm2) ^ ymm6 and both XORs for ymm11, while the remaining add, shift, and store are required.

ff8cbe2794.why: Both reversed vectors must remain in their registers and supply the two stores, so neither shuffle nor store can be removed.

3c39167166.why: The rotate and all three operations implementing the bitwise selection are needed for the preserved RBX and RBP values.

d0aa406e4a.why: The shift and Boolean results are live, and two-operand SSE requires the copy before computing xmm4 while preserving xmm13 and xmm14.

6b16226dc0.why: Every operation feeds a required result, and the two-operand SSE operations need the source-preserving copies.

cde2b15110.why: Both shifts, the add, the AND, and the two XORs contribute to required outputs with no redundant operation.

f5a416f0a2.why: All arithmetic feeds xmm8 or xmm12, and producing xmm8 from preserved xmm10 still needs a copy under two-operand SSE.

41ba7688ee.why: The SHA operations, vector sums, and final copies are all required; sharing the repeated load still requires a replacement copy.

4199aea058.why: Each instruction supplies a required register value or SHA input, including both updates of the implicit xmm0 operand.

67c2870b40.why: The two SHA rounds, their xmm0 setup, the final copy, the xmm2 load/add, and the flag-producing comparison are all needed.

a172b6a294.why: The live sums and Boolean terms require the current operations, including both shift pairs that implement rotations within the allowed ISA.

a4222fded9.why: The two XORs and two additions form the required three-input XOR and sum, and the remaining instructions update required registers.

59ddeec82d.why: All TEST results are overwritten, and the repeated AND masks combine to 0xbe & 0xc3 = 0x82. Keeping ADC first preserves its incoming carry and store, while the single AND produces the same AL and required final flags.

84d0edd7fe.why: OR with the unchanged memory byte is idempotent, and every MOV writes the same constant. One of each preserves CH, the zero-extended RBX value, and all required flags.
